title: Emrys and the Wolf
premise: Sable Okafor, a royal food-taster with a poisoner's constitution and a secret talent for small charms, has survived three years in Vellamere by keeping magic quiet in a city that burns witches. When the old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, Sable's charms start working far too well, drawing the attention of both the Inquisition and Emrys, a wolf-shifter enforcer who serves the outlawed gods. Together they discover that King Aldric died years ago; the thing wearing his crown is a hollow godling feeding on dragon-fire, the last source of true magic, to keep itself alive and the old gods bound. To free the city, Sable must embrace the identity she has hidden, Emrys must choose his duty to the gods over his growing love for her, and together they must unbind the king's corpse from the crown before the last dragon-fire gutters out — succeeding at the cost of the gods' return requiring a new mortal vessel: Sable herself, who accepts on her own terms.
about_author: Tamsin Amberdale is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people whose talents are treated as crimes. She lives near the coast with an ill-tempered cat and an ever-growing collection of folklore collections.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Opening in the royal kitchens, Sable tastes for poison while secretly slipping protective charms into servants' pockets — tiny magics that shouldn't work in a city where the gods have been silent for a century. Tonight one charm flares visibly bright. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine, the first crack in her carefully controlled double life.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A dying child's mother prays to a forgotten river-god, and Emrys, the god's wolf-bound enforcer, feels his master wake for the first time in a hundred years. He tracks the surge of answered magic through Vellamere's rooftops — straight to the palace kitchens. Emotional beat: wary hope; the gods stirring means change, and change means hunters.

chapters.title: The Inquisition Knocks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inquisitor Hale interrogates the kitchen staff after a servant reports glowing charms. Sable lies fluently, but Hale leaves a marked coin as a trap. That night Emrys intercepts her fleeing the palace, offering the gods' protection. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into defiance; two outlaws recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Wolf at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hiding in the temple ruins beneath the city, Sable learns what Emrys is: a mortal bound to serve the sleeping gods, sustained by their fading power. Their uneasy alliance forms over shared exile. Emotional beat: loneliness meeting loneliness; the first spark of trust, and of something warmer neither will name.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The awakened gods show Emrys a vision: King Aldric died three winters ago, and a nameless godling wearing his shape devours dragon-fire to keep the old gods bound and itself immortal. Every prayer since has fed it. Emotional beat: horror and resolve; the enemy is not a tyrant but a hunger enthroned.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following rumors to the royal menagerie, Sable finds the last dragon, ancient and guttering, its fire siphoned nightly to the crown. She bonds with it in stolen visits, her immunity to poison revealed as immunity to its flame. Emotional beat: tenderness and purpose; Sable stops hiding what she is.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Kitchens
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inquisitor Hale catches Sable returning and offers a bargain: betray Emrys or burn. Cornered, Sable gives up a false meeting-place — but Emrys follows her to the exchange anyway and is captured buying her time. Emotional beat: guilt and fury; love against duty cuts both ways now.

chapters.title: The Godling's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Brought before the king-thing, Sable is offered everything she's lost — safety, status, Emrys's life — if she surrenders her flame-immunity to feed the crown. She pretends to accept, learning instead how the binding works: it lives in the coronation oath, spoken over dragon-fire. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the taster knows exactly which ingredient kills.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. During the solstice renewal of the oath, Sable poisons the ritual flame with her own blood-magic while Emrys, escaped by the freed dragon, shatters the oath-circle. The godling unravels; the dead king is released; the old gods rise fully awake — and demand a mortal vessel to walk the world. Emotional beat: triumphant chaos turning to terrible choice.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. Sable accepts godhood on her own terms — not as the gods' puppet but as their voice among mortals, justice outside the law made flesh. Emrys, unbound from servitude, chooses to stay beside her anyway, love no longer at war with duty. The city's magic ban crumbles. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; identity claimed, and a future built rather than inherited.
